title: AI Evals for Cross-Functional Teams — Nachiket Paranjape & Swaroop Chitlur Haridas, DoorDash
talk_summary: DoorDash's GenAI platform team describes an eval platform built API-first with a telemetry layer (traces, scores, observations) and a workflow layer where non-engineers annotate, build golden datasets, and calibrate LLM-as-judge prompts. The key organizational move is enabling strat-ops/PMs to vibe-code their own annotation UIs on top of stable APIs, then self-serve judge calibration with JEPA, cutting annotation cost and iteration time.

takeaways.technique: API-first eval platform with thin vibe-coded UIs
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose scores/datasets/traces as stable table APIs owned by the platform team, then let domain experts use coding agents to build their own annotation UIs on top instead of the platform team building per-use-case UIs.

takeaways.technique: Self-serve LLM-as-judge calibration loop with JEPA
takeaways.what_they_do: Start from a simple judge prompt, score a golden dataset for a baseline, then run an automated prompt-optimization loop (JEPA) and show the original vs calibrated prompt side-by-side for trust before promoting it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we use uh the JPEA library which is a pretty commonly used library out there for prompt optimization

takeaways.technique: Trace → sample → annotate → golden set → calibrate loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Continuously capture agent sessions/traces, sample down to a small reviewable set, annotate with domain knowledge, promote to golden datasets, calibrate judges/agents against them, and repeat.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sampling them down you uh you know to a very small uh set that you actually want to look at uh annotating these with the domain specific expertise

takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly call out that multi-agent systems need trajectory-based evals rather than single-output scoring, judging whole sessions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: with multi- aent systems we needed trajectory based evals

takeaways.technique: Self-serve annotation to cut per-annotation cost
takeaways.what_they_do: Moving annotation into a self-serve platform let teams annotate thousands of rows weekly at lower cost and higher velocity than paid annotators.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we actually did see a lot of reduction in the spend uh at per annotation cost
takeaways.numbers: thousands of rows annotated per week

takeaways.technique: Workflow-first: operators drive platform via coding agents
takeaways.what_they_do: They evolved from UI-first to API-first to workflow-first, letting strat-ops and PMs navigate the platform and run operations themselves through coding agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have become workflow first where we kind of empower SNO and PMs to also being able to uh navigate uh the platform and uh run operations
